body: Cochin Shipyard: IPO 2017 ₹432 (≈₹216 after the 2023 1:1 bonus). ₹112 (May 2020) → ₹2,838 (Jul 2024) ≈25x, with TTM EPS only ~1.3–1.5x and P/E 5.5 → 95, so about 88% of the log-return was rerating. ₹1,138 on 19 Nov 2026 (−60%), EPS falling (₹29.8 → ₹23.8). Mazagon Dock: IPO Oct 2020 ₹145 (≈₹72.5 after the 2024 2:1 split). ₹84 → ₹3,522 (May 2025) ≈42x, EPS ~5.8x, P/E 7.1 → 52. ₹1,850 now (−47%; low −52%). Early signal: in 2020–21 both were net-cash PSUs at 5–8x P/E with dividends, just as defence indigenisation lists and naval programmes (P75 nominated to MDL) gave multi-year visibility. Mazagon's FY23 profit nearly doubled (EPS ₹15 → ₹28), and the stock rose ~380% in the year to Jun 2023. Ended: the P75(I) submarine award (~₹70k–99k cr) kept slipping (still pending in Mar–Aug 2026), meaningful execution is not expected before end-FY28, Cochin's earnings fell, and P/E hit 50–95. Lesson: an order-book narrative rerates a PSU long before earnings arrive. When award timing slips, the rerating unwinds. The EPS-backed one (Mazagon) fell less than the rerating-only one (Cochin).

data.early_signals: net-cash PSUs at 5-8x P/E + indigenisation + naval programmes
data.ended: P75(I) award slippage; Cochin EPS decline
data.note: Prices: screener.in weekly closes, split/bonus-adjusted. P/E = trailing (TTM); implied EPS x = price multiple / P/E multiple.

title: Cochin Shipyard & Mazagon Dock 2020–2025: order-book rerating, then −50–60%
